title: Investigation quickcards for low-slope regressions
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact playbook of quickcards (mini dashboards, queries, and runbook steps) specifically tuned to detect and investigate low-slope regressions — subtle, sustained degradations that are easy to miss with coarse alerting. Goal is to give oncall and owners a fast, repeatable path to triage and remediate without over-alerting.

Context / problem statement:
- We frequently see subtle increases in user-perceived latency, cost per token, or drop in cache effectiveness that accumulate over days. They are often caused by: small model changes, kernel selection drift, micro-changes in request size distributions, slight routing shifts between variants, degradation of KV-cache warmth, or background jobs impacting GPU/IO.
- Traditional threshold alerts (p95 > X) either miss slow drifts or fire too often for transient noise.

Definitions (quick):
- Low-slope regression: a metric shift characterized by a small but persistent change (e.g., 0.2–2% relative change per day) across a rolling window (24–72h) that leads to materially worse SLO burn over 7–14 days.
- Investigation quickcard: a 1–2 panel mini-dashboard + 6–10 step checklist to quickly validate or rule out root causes.

Signal design / metrics to include in every quickcard:
- Rolling-percentiles: p50, p90, p95, p99 on request latency (token-path and end-to-end) at 1m granularity.
- Token-level latencies: per-token generation time distribution (use token-quantiles).
- Cache signals: prefix-cache-hit-rate, kv-cache-hit-rate, cold-cache-request-rate.
- Routing signals: percent of requests routed to fallback/compatible-variant.
- Batch & compile: batch_size_distribution, compile-duration-ms, kernel-fallback-count.
- Request profile: prompt-length-tokens, response-length-tokens, total-model-sequence-length.
- Infra pressure: GPU-utilization-1m, GPU-memory-alloc-fraction, host-load-1m, disk-io-wait.
- Traffic shape: requests-per-second by tenant, weighted by tokens.
- Model artifact: model-version, quantization-tier, kernel-abi-version (as tags).

Detection heuristics (how to flag low-slope regressions):
- Rolling slope detector: compute linear slope over multiple horizons (3h, 24h, 72h) for p95 latency and cache-hit-rate. Flag when slope is positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) across at least two horizons.
- EWMA drift: maintain an EWMA baseline (alpha small, e.g., 0.01) and alert on persistent deviation > relative threshold (e.g., 1.5–3% sustained for 24h).
- CUSUM for small shifts: tuned to detect small mean shifts with low false positives; use separate CUSUM per-tenant.
- Relative tenant deltas: compare per-tenant p95 vs global p95; if a tenant shows sustained >X% divergence, seed targeted tracing.

Tracing heuristics to attach to quickcards:
- Trace anchors to capture: request_id, tenant_id, model_variant, route_policy, batch_id, kv_state (hit/miss), compile_path (fast/slow), kernel-version, fallback-reason.
- Adaptive sampling: increase trace rate for requests in the anomalous cohort (tenant + route + model_variant). For low-slope cases, temporarily bump sampling to 10–20% for impacted cohort for 24–72h to capture distributional shift.
- Focus captures on warm vs cold flows: force traces for first-request-after-idle (to measure prefix-warmth impact) and random warm requests to compare.
- Capture a short token-level timeline (first token, mid-token, tail token durations) for representative traces.

Mini-dashboard (quickcard) layout (2 panels recommended):
Panel A — micro-signal overview (single row time-series, 1h–14d):
- p95 latency (1m), p50, token-mean-latency. Overlay rolling slope (24h) as thin line.
- prefix-cache-hit-rate (1m) stacked below.
- traffic RPS annotated with model-variant percentage.
Query sketch: SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95) as p95 FROM service.requests WHERE env=production TIMESERIES 1m;
Panel B — root-candidate checklist (sparklines per-candidate, 1d–14d):
- GPU util 95th, kernel-fallback-count, batch-size-median, compile-duration-p90, fallback-route-rate.
- Per-tenant delta widget (top 10 tenants by token-volume).

Alert design (soft, staged):
- Stage 1 (info): Rolling-slope-warning: slope(p95, 24h) > 0.5% AND slope(p95, 72h) > 0.3% -> create ticket but no pager.
- Stage 2 (investigate): EWMA deviation > 2% sustained for 24h OR tenant delta > 5% for >12h -> email oncall + create investigation quickcard link.
- Stage 3 (pager): absolute p95 breach that impacts SLO (e.g., p95 > SLA threshold) or simultaneous infra pressure (GPU util > 90%) -> page SRE.
Rationale: avoid noisy pages, give teams a chance to observe and roll back canary changes.

Runbook quick steps (6–10 steps, copyable into pager ticket):
1) Confirm signal: open quickcard (Panel A/B), verify slope is consistent across 3h/24h/72h.
2) Scope: is it global, region, model-variant, or tenant-specific? Use per-tenant delta widget.
3) Correlate: check recent rollouts (product/serving), kernel upgrades, quantization changes, or infra maintenance windows. Linked swarm: github PRs + release tags.
4) Trace sample pull: for impacted cohort, query traces (increase sampling if needed) and inspect anchor fields: cache state, batch_id, compile-duration.
5) Compare warm vs cold: compute p95 for requests with prefix_cache_hit=true vs false.
6) Infra check: GPU host metrics, autoscaler events, queue-length and backlog.
7) Quick mitigations: temporarily route heavy-tenants to alternative compatible-variant; rollback recent rollout; increase cache prefetch for high-volume prefixes.
8) Post-mortem seeds: snapshot quickcard, attach traces, list hypothesis, assign owner for RCA.

Investigation examples (hypotheses and how to validate):
- Hypothesis A: kernel selection change increased per-token compile-time. Validate: look at kernel-version tag over time + compile-duration-p90.
- Hypothesis B: distribution shift -> more long prompts leading to increased batch fragmentation. Validate: prompt-length-tokens distribution + batch_size_median.
- Hypothesis C: KV cache churn -> lower prefix-hit-rate correlated with latency. Validate: prefix-cache-hit-rate vs p95 aligned time windows.

Example queries and snippets (sketches to copy into query UI):
- Per-tenant delta: SELECT tenant_id, percentile(latency_ms,95) as p95 FROM requests WHERE env=prod GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY token_volume DESC LIMIT 20;
- Slope calc (pseudocode): SLOPE = linear_regression_slope(timeseries(window=24h)); alert if SLOPE>THRESH and pvalue<0.05;
- Cache comparison: SELECT percentile(latency_ms,95) FROM requests WHERE prefix_cache_hit = true; then same where false.

Sampling knobs (practical):
- Baseline trace rate: 0.5% global.
- Anomalous cohort rate: 10–20% for 24–72h.
- Warm/cold seeding: ensure at least 200 warm and 200 cold traces per 24h when investigating.

Ownership and escalation matrix:
- SRE/ops: owns detection pipeline and alerting thresholds, initial triage.
- Observability product: owns quickcard templates & dashboard maintenance.
- Serving-runtime: owns kernel selection, batching, compile-path investigations.
- Solutions/SE: owns tenant communication and routing decisions for high-touch customers.

Backtesting & tuning notes (action items):
- We need a small notebook to backtest slope and EWMA thresholds on 2024–2025 production windows (Marco).
- Add unit tests / synthetic injection harness to validate CUSUM sensitivity (Aisha).
- Add a scheduled weekly report of ‘small but sustained metric drifts’ to product-metrics (owner: Nikhil).

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is an acceptable false-positive rate for slope alerts? propose target: 1/month per service.
- Where to store quickcard templates? (confluence vs dashboard-library) - prefer dashboard-library for direct links.
- Should we store sampled trace cohorts for 14 days by default? cost tradeoffs to discuss with finance.

Notes to self / informal reminders:
- Keep quickcards lightweight — 2 panels, clear copy, link to runbook.
- When in doubt, seed traces for both warm and cold flows to rule out cache-driven regressions quickly.
- Avoid paging for tiny slope signals — ticket + observation window is usually enough.

Appendix (links to relevant artifacts):
- Telemetry repo PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/218 (sampling knobs)
- Recent canary history: JIRA-DEPLOY-2026-011 (check 2026-02-10 kernel rollout)

End of quickcard playbook.
